canonical_question: What is the specific cause for the broad particle size distribution (10 to 300 μm) in atomized powder compared to the narrow distribution of milled powders?

question_variants.question: What is the specific cause for the broad particle size distribution (10 to 300 μm) in atomized powder compared to the narrow distribution of milled powders?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document states the atomized (AT) powder has a broad particle size distribution (10-300 μm) compared to milled powders, but does not explain the specific cause for this broad distribution.

answers.answer: The text reports the AT powder has a broad distribution from 10 to 300 μm resulting from crucible-free electrode induction-melting gas atomization, but does not explain the physical cause of this specific broad range.
answers.boundary_limitation: No cause for distribution width provided.
evidence_spans: atomized powder (AT) prepared from arc melted HfNbTaTiZr alloy by crucible-free electrode induction-melting gas atomization in a protective Ar atmosphere to suppress undesirable oxidation.
The AT powder had a broad particle size distribution covering the range from 10 to 300 μm.
MA and AT powders were compacted by SPS in an SPS 10-4 device (Santa Rosa, California, CA, USA) using a graphite die (Ø 20 mm) and punches to compact the powder using pressure of 80 MPa.
